source_findings: Published conductivity is divided by 1000 to W/(mm K); Celsius increments are valid for this steady conduction-only problem. F has units W/mm, axial flux W/mm2 and area-scaled power W.

Positive piecewise-linear conductivity makes F strictly increasing. Segment primitive k_i*dt+m_i*dt^2/2 and stable inverse 2s/(k_i+sqrt(k_i^2+2m_i*s)) are consistent for positive, negative and zero slopes.
Literal totals Z=37.10525 and XY=35.0315 W/mm imply axial fluxes -3.710525/-3.50315 W/mm2 and cold/hot outward powers +7.42105/-7.42105 and +7.0063/-7.0063 W.

The oracle strictly refuses nonfinite, Boolean and outside-range temperature/position values. It does not clamp. Numerical Decimal inversion is a 60-digit reference, not an exactly representable algebraic temperature.

Drafts specify the same assumed 1x2x10 mm, 16 HEX8 bar, 68 nodes/60 free scalar DOFs, in-range linear initial field and 23/250 C end values. Separate XY override changes only its column and output base.
